title: Technical English — Course 4, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 2

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the multimeter lesson take place?
tasks.audioText: The metrology instructor will demonstrate how to read a digital multimeter display on Thursday at one fifteen. Students will work with printed examples and identify the unit shown for each measurement. The instructor will explain the difference between voltage, current and resistance. The class will not involve live circuit testing.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. What will students identify on the display?
tasks.audioText: The metrology instructor will demonstrate how to read a digital multimeter display on Thursday at one fifteen. Students will work with printed examples and identify the unit shown for each measurement. The instructor will explain the difference between voltage, current and resistance. The class will not involve live circuit testing.
options: The unit shown for each measurement

tasks.prompt: An electrical measurement record should include the measured value, the unit and enough context to identify the test point. Voltage is measured in volts, current in amperes and resistance in ohms. A technician should also record the instrument identification when the procedure requires it. Writing a number without a unit can make a result unclear or misleading. Reading 1. Which unit is used for resistance?
Why should a measurement include its unit?
options: To make the result clear and avoid misunderstanding

tasks.prompt: Choose TWO details that should appear in a clear electrical measurement record.
options: The colour of the instrument case

tasks.prompt: The standard unit of electrical resistance is the ___.
A measurement value has no unit. What should you ask?
options: I will assume the unit from the number.
Could you confirm the unit and test point for this measurement?
I will add any unit I prefer.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of measuring electrical values in a logical order.
options: Record the test point and instrument details
correctOrder: Record the test point and instrument details

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words explaining why electrical measurement records need values, units and test-point information.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: task completion and relevant content (0–2); clear organisation and logical linking (0–2); grammar and sentence structure (0–2); accurate electrical vocabulary, spelling and punctuation (0–2). Minor errors are acceptable if meaning remains clear.
